title: Make the settlement report say what went wrong

blocks.text: The finance team reads the nightly settlement report every morning. It has one line per merchant, and each merchant's day is settled with its bank on a pool, all at once. The line for every merchant whose bank call went wrong reads `failed: ExecutionException`, so nobody can tell a bank that timed out from a bug in the ledger. And on the night the ledger database ran out of connections, the report job died after the first failing merchant, and nobody got a report.
`run(...)` already submits the settlements and builds the report. Finish the `TODO` in `src/main/java/practice/SettlementReport.java`:

items: `line(...)`: wait for one merchant's settlement and write its line.

blocks.text: When you're done, a failed merchant's line names what the bank call threw and its message, every merchant gets its line whatever happened to the others, and stopping the report job while it waits ends the job instead of filling the report with failures. About six lines in total.
The tests settle merchants on a real `ExecutorService`.

cases.says: every merchant the bank settled gets a line with its amount, in the order the merchants were given
a failed settlement is reported as the exception the bank call threw, with its message
a merchant whose settlement failed still gets its line, and so do the merchants after it
an interrupt of the thread waiting for the report ends the report with InterruptedException instead of being reported as a merchant's failure

origin.section: A Callable's Result and Its Exception Both Come Back Through get()

concepts: Whatever a task throws comes back from get() as an ExecutionException whose cause is the original exception.
InterruptedException from get() means the waiting thread was interrupted, not that the task failed.
